problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(x+2)(2-y).$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)<0?$
worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=-2$ and $y=2.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have a strict inequality, we use dashed lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/38f5235039b0a5800651759e8da98166451ab72d25e7eaa9772c10b68c3618ff.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/a68d4ca3939349cef83c3c84117df44ddacf49d587b1bc8a871918f62d9b6516.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x+2)$ | $(2-y)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-left | $(-3,3)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(-1,3)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-3,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(-1,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)<0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/1055b7667e7b1c6d27ad7a9d28ec74ae7ed58dac262ae83b5c4028dcee3f9312.png)
